title: [Feature Request] Support SAO-style single-rollout asynchronous optimization for agentic RL
bodyExcerpt:
### Motivation
GRPO's group-wise sampling seems mismatched with asynchronous agentic RL — the group must wait for the slowest rollout, causing stale data and off-policy drift (the SAO paper reports collapse at ~160 async steps).
SAO (https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.07508) (Tsinghua/GLM team, deployed in GLM-5.2 750B) addresses this with one rollout per prompt + critic, achieving stable training for ~1000 steps and +6 points on SWE-Bench Verified over stabilized GRPO.
I'm wondering if the team would consider supporting this paradigm in verl?
### What SAO does
1. Single-rollout (group size=1): each trajectory trains immediately, no group barrier
2. DIS clipping: use π_rollout directly (drop π_θ_old), mask tokens outside [1-ε_ℓ, 1+ε_h] entirely
3. Faster + frozen-attention critic: K=2 critic updates per policy update; freeze attention layers (only train MoE/MLP)
4. Skip-observation GAE: skip env observation tokens in advantage computation, link action-end → next-action-start

title: [roadmap] verl 26Q3 roadmap
